```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(ggplot2)
out <- params$out
rd <- function(f) if (file.exists(file.path(out, f))) read.csv(file.path(out, f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) else NULL
drift_src <- file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "..", "..", "src", "harmonization", "drift")
source(file.path(drift_src, "drift_models.R")); source(file.path(drift_src, "drift_biology.R"))
source(file.path(drift_src, "drift_partition.R")); source(file.path(drift_src, "drift_stats.R"))
source(file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "partition_plots.R"))
tt <- rd("tubes.csv"); dec <- rd("decisions.csv"); eff <- read_effects(out)
cfg <- if (nzchar(params$config) && file.exists(params$config)) yaml::read_yaml(params$config) else NULL
if (!is.null(cfg) && !is.null(cfg$technical_markers)) PARTITION_CONTROL_MARKERS <- unlist(cfg$technical_markers)
cs <- function(x) paste(unlist(x), collapse = ", ")

# One visual system for every figure: instruments are identities (fixed categorical order, reference
# first), verdicts are statuses (detected effects in colour, the rest grey), signed effects use a
# blue-grey-red diverging scale and magnitudes a single blue ramp.
ref <- if (!is.null(cfg)) cfg$reference_instrument else NA
instr_levels <- if (!is.null(tt)) c(intersect(ref, unique(tt$instrument)), setdiff(sort(unique(tt$instrument)), ref)) else character(0)
pal_instr <- setNames(c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#4a3aa7", "#e34948")[seq_along(instr_levels)], instr_levels)
verdict_levels <- c("negligible", "inconclusive", "not detected", "detected, relevance unknown", "detected, not clinically relevant",
                    "detected, within counting noise", "detected, correct")   # "not detected": decisions written before 2026-10-13
pal_verdict <- setNames(c("#c9c9c4", "#9a9a94", "#9a9a94", "#eda100", "#eda100", "#eda100", "#e34948"), verdict_levels)
shape_verdict <- setNames(c(1, 16, 16, 17, 15, 0, 18), verdict_levels)
thm <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
  strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0ee", colour = NA), legend.position = "bottom",
  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = .5, hjust = 1, size = 7))
layer_lab <- c(A = "A technical", BG = "BG background", B = "B endpoint")
if (!is.null(dec)) {
  dec$verdict <- factor(dec$verdict, verdict_levels)
  dec$layer_f <- factor(layer_lab[dec$layer], layer_lab)
  unit_sd <- if ("margin" %in% names(dec)) dec$margin else dec$replicate_sd   # effect in units of the rule 1 margin
  dec$z <- dec$effect_mean / unit_sd
  dec$z_lo <- dec$ci_low / unit_sd; dec$z_hi <- dec$ci_high / unit_sd
}
if (!is.null(tt)) tt$instrument <- factor(tt$instrument, instr_levels)
```

Plans: `docs/plans/drift_three_questions_plan.md` (the three questions below), `docs/plans/mtb_batch_drift_plan.md` (the decision rule).

```{r answers-setup}
vp <- read_partition(out); vp_all <- read_partition(out, variant = NULL)
# the responder call is a decision, not a data setting: fitted for the record, left out of every comparison
if (!is.null(vp)) vp <- vp[vp$representation %in% compared_reps(), ]
if (!is.null(vp_all)) vp_all <- vp_all[vp_all$representation %in% compared_reps(), ]
vp_engine <- if (!is.null(vp)) vp$engine[1] else NA
calls <- rd("calls_compare.csv"); agree <- rd("calls_agreement.csv")
pal_group <- c(unwanted = "#e34948", wanted = "#2a78d6", residual = "#c9c9c4")
rep_label <- vapply(PARTITION_REPS, `[[`, "", "label")
# "cocktail used or not" is one factor for the reader: the stimulated contrast plus the pool term (the neg is a pool level)
merge_cocktail <- function(sh) { sh$factor[sh$factor %in% c("stimulated", "pool")] <- "cocktail"; aggregate(share ~ readout + representation + factor + group, sh, sum) }
fac_order <- function(f) { tech <- c(unlist(cfg$design$technical)); unique(c(intersect(c(tech, "acq_day"), f), setdiff(f, c(tech, "residual")), "residual")) }
```

## What was run

Every tube is turned into readouts (the frequency of each cytokine gate in CD4 and CD8, and the MFI of each marker); each readout is prepared in several settings (MFI linear or arcsinh; frequency as %, arcsinh or logit; each plain or with the visit's unstimulated tube subtracted); and for every readout and setting one model splits the differences between tubes into batch (acquisition day, instrument, operator), biology (patient, weeks since vaccination, prior vaccination, peptide pool) and an unexplained rest. The best setting keeps the most biology and the least batch.

```{r explain, fig.width=15, fig.height=3.4}
print(plot_explain_workflow())
```

```{r explain-example, fig.width=12, fig.height=9}
fq_x <- rd("gated_frequencies.csv"); if (!is.null(fq_x) && !is.null(tt)) print(plot_explain_example(fq_x, read.csv(file.path(out, "tubes.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE), "CD4:IFNg"))
```

```{r explain-scorecard, fig.width=11, fig.height=5.5}
if (!is.null(vp)) print(plot_explain_scorecard(vp))
```

## How this compares with published work

DOIs checked by literature search on 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13.

| Finding here | Published support | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| MFI is mostly batch (acquisition day); gated frequencies are much less affected | Supported: across sites, instruments and years, frequency CVs are 2 to 4 times lower than MFI CVs, and MFI needs bead or target-value calibration to be comparable | Leipold et al. 2018 (10.1016/j.jim.2017.11.008); Le Lann et al. 2020 (10.1038/s41598-020-68468-3); Solly et al. 2019 (10.1002/cyto.a.23844); Glier et al. 2019 (10.1016/j.jim.2017.07.013); Kalina et al. 2012 (10.1038/leu.2012.122) |
| Splitting the variance of logit frequencies into technical and biological parts with a mixed model | Same method: the HIPC multicentre study (centre, sample, residual on logit proportions); repeat runs of one donation give technical CVs of 12 to 101 percent, mostly below the biological variance | Finak et al. 2016 (10.1038/srep20686); Burel et al. 2017 (10.4049/jimmunol.1601750) |
| Subtracting the unstimulated tube removes day variance but adds noise | Supported in principle: modelling stimulated and unstimulated counts together beats subtraction, ratios and Fisher's test (the "frequency logit stim/neg" setting follows this) | Finak et al. 2014, MIMOSA (10.1093/biostatistics/kxt024); Lin et al. 2015, COMPASS (10.1038/nbt.3187) |
| "Patient" partly reflects sample quality (negative control on lineage, viability and scatter markers) | Supported: time to freezing, thawing, resting and viability change ICS stimulated-vs-unstimulated readouts without changing the cells themselves | Bull et al. 2007 (10.1016/j.jim.2007.02.003); Weinberg et al. 2009 (10.1128/CVI.00342-08); Kutscher et al. 2013 (10.1371/journal.pone.0076215); Horton et al. 2007 (10.1016/j.jim.2007.03.002) |
| Gating counts as a technical factor | Supported: gating was the largest controllable source of ICS variability between laboratories. Here one person gated every tube, so the low batch share of the frequencies may not carry over to multi-analyst gating | Maecker et al. 2005 (10.1186/1471-2172-6-13); Welters et al. 2012 (10.1007/s00262-012-1282-9) |
| Comparing linear and arcsinh MFI, %, arcsinh % and logit, each with and without subtraction, by biological against batch share | No direct precedent found. Transformation studies judge gating quality or variance stabilisation, not this split; the arcsinh cofactor matters per channel | Finak et al. 2010 (10.1186/1471-2105-11-546); Azad et al. 2016, flowVS (10.1186/s12859-016-1083-9) |
| Lineage and viability markers used as a negative control for the patient factor | No direct precedent found; closest are viability-dye controls and spiked reference samples | Horton et al. 2007; Schuyler et al. 2019 (10.3389/fimmu.2019.02367) |

## Answer 1: do the data need correcting?

Each technical contrast (every acquisition day, the instrument, every operator) is tested in three layers: technical markers of the unstimulated tubes (A), the background of the unstimulated tubes (BG) and the endpoints (B). Rule 1 has three states against a relevance margin: for counts (layers BG and B) a shift of log(1 + `r if (!is.null(cfg$relevance$count_cv)) cfg$relevance$count_cv else 0.35`) on the logit scale, the inter-laboratory CV of ICS responses (Jaimes et al. 2011); for the technical markers and intensities the noise between tubes of the same sample. An effect is *detected* when it exceeds the margin with posterior probability of at least `r if (!is.null(cfg)) cfg$replicate_noise_prob else 0.95`, *negligible* when it stays inside with that probability, and *inconclusive* otherwise (Kruschke 2018). Rule 2: removing the effect changes more responder calls than counting noise alone changes on the same tubes (the 95th percentile of binomial resampling); the flip count is averaged over posterior draws. A correction is warranted only when both hold (CLSI H62; O'Hara et al. 2011 for intermediate precision across operators, days and instruments).

```{r answer1}
if (!is.null(dec)) {
  cs1 <- correction_summary(dec)
  knitr::kable(cs1, caption = "Technical contrasts per term and layer: detected above noise (rule 1) and flipping responder calls (rule 2)", row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r answer1-line, results="asis"}
if (!is.null(dec)) {
  fl <- dec[dec$verdict %in% "detected, correct", ]
  n_inc <- sum(dec$verdict %in% "inconclusive")
  if (!nrow(fl)) cat("**No correction needed.** No technical effect both exceeds the margin and changes more responder calls than counting noise. Keep the technical factors as covariates in downstream models.\n\n")
  else { cat(sprintf("**Correction to consider for %d contrast(s)**, each flipping more responder calls than counting noise:\n\n", nrow(fl)))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(fl))) cat(sprintf("- %s %s = %s (layer %s): %.1f call(s) on average (95%% interval %.0f to %.0f; counting noise alone: 95th percentile %.0f)\n",
      fl$response[i], fl$term[i], fl$level[i], fl$layer[i], fl$positivity_flips[i], fl$flips_lo[i], fl$flips_hi[i], fl$noise_flips_q95[i]))
    cat("\nFlipping calls on a single response may also be handled by flagging those calls rather than correcting values.\n\n") }
  if (n_inc) cat(sprintf("%d of %d contrasts are **inconclusive**: their posterior reaches both inside and beyond the margin, so the data cannot say whether they matter. Most are days with one patient.\n\n", n_inc, nrow(dec)))
}
```

## Answer 2: should the unstimulated tube be subtracted?

The same endpoints prepared in different ways, each fitted with every factor: as percentages, arcsinh or logit, each plain and with the unstimulated tube subtracted (for logit: the stimulated counts over the neg as an offset, the MIMOSA idea of modelling both together). The responder call is not one of these settings: it is a decision made from the data, compared separately below. A representation is better when its unwanted share falls and its wanted share does not (the batch-removal against biological-conservation trade-off of Luecken et al. 2022). Shares are of the between-tube variance on each representation's own scale.

```{r answer2, results="asis"}
if (!is.null(vp)) {
  st2 <- subtraction_table(vp)
  if (!is.null(st2)) {
    st2$alternative <- rep_label[st2$alternative]
    print(knitr::kable(st2[, -2], digits = 2, caption = paste("Question 2 per readout, against the gated counts on the logit scale (engine:", vp_engine, ")"), row.names = FALSE))
    cat("\n"); print(knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(st2$alternative, st2$verdict)), caption = "Readouts per verdict"))
  }
}
```

### All combinations of gating level and data setting

Two choices shape every readout: where in the gating hierarchy it is taken (no gate, live cells or the CD4 or CD8 gate for intensities; the manual FlowJo cytokine gate for frequencies) and how it is prepared (scale, and whether the unstimulated tube is subtracted). Every combination is fitted with every factor. The biological share sums patient, weeks since vaccination, prior vaccination and cocktail (used or not, which pool); the batch share sums acquisition day, instrument and operator. Values are medians over the cytokine readouts of each combination; the lineage, viability and scatter markers are negative controls and are only shown per readout.

A combination is dropped when it has more batch than biological variance, or when another combination has at least as much biology and at most as much batch.

```{r grid-combinations, fig.width=15, fig.height=5.5, results="asis"}
if (!is.null(vp)) {
  print(plot_combinations(vp))
  gs <- partition_grid(vp, summary = TRUE); gs$setting <- gsub("\n", " ", gs$setting)
  print(knitr::kable(gs[, c("kind", "gating", "setting", "biological_pct", "batch_pct", "unexplained_pct", "bio_minus_batch", "n_readouts", "verdict", "better")],
        digits = 1, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Median percent of variance per combination and its verdict (partition_grid_summary.csv; per readout in partition_grid.csv)"))
}
```

```{r grid-paired, fig.width=15, fig.height=6}
if (!is.null(vp)) { print(plot_partition_paired(vp, "freq")); print(plot_partition_paired(vp, "mfi")) }
```

```{r grid-full, fig.width=13, fig.height=6}
if (!is.null(vp)) { print(plot_partition_full(vp, "freq")); print(plot_partition_full(vp, "mfi")) }
```

The markers measured on all live cells (CD4, CD8, live/dead, cell size and granularity) are a negative control for the subtraction: the peptide is not expected to change them, so after "stimulated minus unstimulated" their biological share should be close to zero and their remaining batch share shows what subtraction cannot remove. They appear in the per-readout figures.

### Do the two fitting engines agree?

Every model was fitted twice: with brms (Bayesian, the source of every figure above) and with lme4 (classical, fast). Points on the diagonal mean both engines attribute the same share to that source.

```{r grid-engines, fig.width=14, fig.height=11, results="asis"}
ea <- plot_engine_agreement(out)
if (!is.null(ea)) { print(ea$plot); print(knitr::kable(ea$table, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Agreement per setting: correlation of the shares and median / largest difference in percentage points")) }
```

```{r grid-readout, fig.width=15, fig.height=24}
if (!is.null(vp)) { print(plot_partition_paired(vp, "freq", by_readout = TRUE)); print(plot_partition_paired(vp, "mfi", by_readout = TRUE)) }
```

```{r answer2-calls, fig.width=11, fig.height=5, results="asis"}
if (!is.null(agree)) print(knitr::kable(agree, digits = 2, caption = "Positive calls per rule and agreement (Cohen's kappa). Lab rule: subtracted frequency and fold over neg; Fisher: one-sided exact test, BH q < 0.05 (Horton et al. 2007); MIMOSA: Finak et al. 2014", row.names = FALSE))
if (!is.null(calls)) {
  calls$agreement <- ifelse(calls$lab & calls$fisher, "both", ifelse(calls$lab, "lab only", ifelse(calls$fisher, "Fisher only", "neither")))
  print(ggplot(calls, aes(pmax(neg_pct, 1e-3), pmax(pct, 1e-3), colour = agreement)) + geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "#9a9a94") +
    geom_point(alpha = .6, size = 1.2) + scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() + facet_wrap(~response, ncol = 4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(both = "#2a78d6", "lab only" = "#eda100", "Fisher only" = "#e34948", neither = "#c9c9c4")) + thm +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0)) + labs(x = "matched neg %", y = "stimulated %", colour = NULL,
    title = "Stimulated against unstimulated frequency, by calling rule (after Finak et al. 2014)"))
}
```

## Answer 3: where do the differences between tubes come from?

Share of the between-tube variance per factor, for every readout and representation, from one model per readout with all factors (variance partition after Hoffman & Schadt 2016; the cytometry precedent is the multicentre mixed model of Finak et al. 2016). Unwanted factors in red, wanted in blue. Fixed factors contribute the variance of their part of the prediction, random factors their variance (Nakagawa et al. 2017). Instrument and operator are largely nested in acquisition day and calendar period, so the split among the three unwanted factors is approximate; their total is robust (see the comparison without operator below).

The figures for this question are in "All settings compared" above (per setting and per readout). Totals with 95 percent intervals:

```{r answer3-totals}
if (!is.null(vp)) {
  tw <- reshape(vp[vp$factor %in% c("total_unwanted", "total_wanted"), c("readout", "representation", "factor", "share", "lo", "hi")],
                idvar = c("readout", "representation"), timevar = "factor", direction = "wide")
  knitr::kable(tw, digits = 2, caption = "Batch (unwanted) and biological (wanted) totals with 95 percent intervals", row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r answer3-guard}
if (!is.null(vp_all) && any(vp_all$variant != "full")) {
  g <- vp_all[vp_all$factor %in% c("total_unwanted", "total_wanted", "acq_day", "instrument", unlist(cfg$design$technical)), ]
  gw <- reshape(g[, c("readout", "representation", "variant", "factor", "share")], idvar = c("readout", "representation", "factor"), timevar = "variant", direction = "wide")
  names(gw) <- sub("^share\\.", "", names(gw))
  knitr::kable(gw[gw$factor %in% c("total_unwanted", "acq_day"), ], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = "Confounding guard (lme4): unwanted total and day share with and without operator. A day share that grows by what operator loses shows the two cannot be separated")
}
```

## Acquisition audit: what else differs between tubes, and what can be modelled

Step 11b reads every FCS keyword, the FlowJo workspaces and the gate counts. A source can only be a separate term of the variance partition if no other term already determines it; otherwise the model cannot tell the two apart and gives one of them all the variance. The overlap figure shows, for every pair, how much knowing one factor determines the other.

| Source | Overlap | How it is used |
|---|---|---|
| Detector voltages, compensation matrix, CS&T setup | almost fully determined by the acquisition day | not a model term: they explain why days differ (figure: voltages over time) |
| Instrument, operator | largely determined by the day and the calendar period | model terms; their split from the day is approximate, the batch total is robust |
| Visit (one patient at one week) | determines day, week and patient | its own category, neither batch nor biology: it holds both sample handling and visit-level biology |
| Sample quality (viability, live cells) | measured on the visit's unstimulated tube; mostly explained by day and visit | technical term at the visit level (the peptide does not change viability) |
| Gate position | determined by the day and the voltages, and set after looking at the data | not a model term (it would count the day twice and adjust for a consequence of the data); shown as a diagnostic |
| Counting noise | computed from the cell counts, independent of every factor | split out of the unexplained variance |

```{r audit, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, results="asis"}
if (!is.null(fo)) { M <- as.matrix(fo[, -1]); rownames(M) <- fo[[1]]; colnames(M) <- names(read.csv(file.path(out, "factor_overlap.csv"), check.names = FALSE))[-1]; print(plot_factor_overlap(M)) }

if (!is.null(ft)) {

  print(knitr::kable(tab[order(tab$parameter, -tab$samples), ], row.names = FALSE,
    caption = "FlowJo display transformations of the fluorescence channels: samples per setting (a display setting changes where a gate is drawn, not the data)"))
```


## Technical precision against clinical targets

Technical CV implied by the unwanted variance on the log-like scales (arcsinh MFI, logit of a frequency): sqrt(exp(v) - 1). Targets: CV at most 25 percent, at most 30 to 35 percent for rare events (CLSI H62; O'Hara et al. 2011). Inter-laboratory ICS precision for orientation: about 70 percent CV for responses at or below 0.1 percent and about 20 percent above 0.5 percent (Maecker et al. 2005, Table 2).

```{r precision, results="asis"}
if (!is.null(vp)) {
  lv <- vp[vp$representation %in% c("mfi_asinh", "freq_raw", "freq_ratio") & vp$factor == "total_unwanted", ]
  lv$technical_cv <- technical_cv(lv$variance)
  lv$target <- ifelse(lv$technical_cv <= .25, "within 25 %", ifelse(lv$technical_cv <= .35, "within 35 % (rare events)", "above 35 %"))
  if (!is.null(fqp <- rd("gated_frequencies.csv"))) {
    med <- aggregate(pct ~ readout, transform(fqp[!fqp$is_neg, ], readout = paste(parent, gate, sep = ":")), median); names(med)[2] <- "median_stim_pct"
    lv <- merge(lv, med, by = "readout", all.x = TRUE)
  }
  lv$representation <- rep_label[lv$representation]
  print(knitr::kable(lv[, intersect(c("readout", "representation", "median_stim_pct", "share", "technical_cv", "target"), names(lv))], digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
                     caption = "Technical CV implied by the unwanted variance (instrument, day, operator) against the CLSI H62 / O'Hara targets"))
}
```

```{r levey-jennings, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
ns_all <- rd("neg_summaries.csv")
if (!is.null(ns_all) && !is.null(tt) && !is.null(cfg)) {
  op <- setdiff(design_technical_factors(cfg), "instrument")[1]
  nt <- merge(ns_all[ns_all$marker %in% cfg$technical_markers, ], tt[tt$is_neg %in% TRUE, intersect(c("filename", "acq_day", "instrument", op), names(tt))], by = "filename")
  nt$operator <- if (!is.na(op) && op %in% names(nt)) nt[[op]] else "not recorded"
  dm <- aggregate(median ~ marker + acq_day + instrument + operator, nt, mean)
  lim <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(dm, dm$marker), function(x) data.frame(marker = x$marker[1], m = mean(x$median), s = sd(x$median))))
  print(ggplot(dm, aes(acq_day, median)) + geom_hline(data = lim, aes(yintercept = m), colour = "#52514e") +
    geom_hline(data = lim, aes(yintercept = m - 2 * s), linetype = 2, colour = "#9a9a94") + geom_hline(data = lim, aes(yintercept = m + 2 * s), linetype = 2, colour = "#9a9a94") +
    geom_line(aes(group = 1), colour = "#c9c9c4") + geom_point(aes(colour = instrument, shape = factor(operator)), size = 2.2) +
    facet_wrap(~marker, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) + scale_colour_manual(values = pal_instr) + thm +
    labs(x = "acquisition day", y = "mean of neg-tube medians", colour = NULL, shape = "operator",
         title = "Levey-Jennings view of the unstimulated tubes: day mean and +/- 2 SD (after Perfetto et al. 2012)"))
}
```

## Biological effect: weeks since first vaccination

The headline of this analysis is biology: the change of every endpoint response with time since first vaccination (fixed week slope, logit per year, lme4 glmer with the endpoint design plus the fixed slope). Each slope is estimated twice, with the full design and with the technical terms removed (no instrument contrast, no acquisition-day intercept). If the two agree, technical drift is not what the response is measuring. Below, the full model is refitted with each acquisition day left out in turn, and the per-patient slopes (fixed plus random) are shown by group.

```{r, results="asis"}
sens <- rd("week_slope_sensitivity.csv"); lodo <- rd("week_slope_lodo.csv"); subj <- rd("week_slope_subjects.csv")
pal_model <- c(full = "#2a78d6", no_technical = "#1baf7a")
if (!is.null(sens) && !is.null(lodo)) cat(sensitivity_sentence(sens), lodo_sentence(lodo, sens), "\n")
```

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
if (!is.null(sens)) {
  sp <- sens[is.finite(sens$week_slope), ]
  sp$model <- factor(sp$model, names(pal_model)); sp$lo <- sp$week_slope - 1.96 * sp$se; sp$hi <- sp$week_slope + 1.96 * sp$se
  sp$response <- factor(sp$response, rev(unique(sp$response[sp$model == "full"][order(sp$week_slope[sp$model == "full"])])))
  print(ggplot(sp, aes(week_slope, response, colour = model)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#52514e") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, linewidth = .6, position = position_dodge(.55)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.6, position = position_dodge(.55)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal_model, labels = c(full = "full design", no_technical = "without technical terms"), drop = FALSE) +
    thm + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = .5)) +
    labs(x = "week slope, logit per year (estimate and 95% interval)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
         title = "Change of the endpoint responses over time, with and without the technical terms"))
} else cat("week_slope_sensitivity.csv not present (run scripts/drift/06_biology.R)\n")
```

```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=7.5}
if (!is.null(lodo) && !is.null(sens)) {
  ls <- lodo_shifts(lodo, sens); ls <- ls[is.finite(ls$week_slope), ]
  full <- unique(ls[, c("response", "week_slope_full", "se_full")])
  print(ggplot(ls, aes(dropped_day, week_slope)) +
    geom_rect(data = full, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = week_slope_full - se_full, ymax = week_slope_full + se_full), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#f0f0ee") +
    geom_hline(data = full, aes(yintercept = week_slope_full), colour = pal_model[["full"]], linewidth = .8) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#52514e", linetype = 2) +
    geom_point(colour = "#9a9a94", size = 1.6) +
    geom_point(data = ls[ls$flag, ], colour = "#eb6834", size = 2.2) +
    geom_text(data = ls[ls$flag, ], aes(label = dropped_day), colour = "#eb6834", size = 2.4, angle = 90,
              hjust = ifelse(ls$shift_se[ls$flag] > 0, -0.25, 1.25)) +
    facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = .55)) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + thm +
    labs(x = "acquisition day left out", y = "week slope, logit per year",
         title = "Leave-one-day-out: blue line and band are the full-model slope and its SE; labelled days move it by more than one SE"))
} else cat("week_slope_lodo.csv not present (run scripts/drift/06_biology.R)\n")
```

```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.5}
if (!is.null(subj)) {
  grp <- if (!is.null(tt) && "prior_vacc" %in% names(tt)) unique(tt[, c("patient", "prior_vacc")]) else NULL
  subj$patient <- as.character(subj$patient)
  if (!is.null(grp)) { grp$patient <- as.character(grp$patient); subj <- merge(subj, grp, by = "patient", all.x = TRUE); subj$group <- factor(paste("prior_vacc =", subj$prior_vacc)) }

    geom_jitter(width = .18, height = 0, size = 1.8, alpha = .85) +
```

## Decisions

Every effect is shown in units of the same-day replicate noise of that response, so scatter, arcsinh and logit responses share one axis. Rule 1 asks whether the effect exceeds one replicate SD with posterior probability above the configured threshold (dashed lines at plus and minus 1). Rule 2 counts positivity calls that change when the effect is removed.

```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
if (!is.null(dec)) {
  di <- dec[dec$term != "day" & is.finite(dec$z), ]
  di$contrast <- ifelse(di$term == "instrument", as.character(di$level), paste0(di$term, ": ", di$level))
  di$response <- factor(di$response, rev(unique(di$response[order(di$layer, di$z)])))
  print(ggplot(di, aes(z, response, colour = verdict, shape = verdict)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#52514e") + geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = 2, colour = "#9a9a94") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = z_lo, xmax = z_hi), height = 0, linewidth = .5) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    facet_grid(layer_f ~ contrast, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    scale_x_continuous(trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 1), breaks = c(-30, -10, -3, -1, 0, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal_verdict, drop = FALSE) + scale_shape_manual(values = shape_verdict, drop = FALSE) +
    thm + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = .5)) +
    labs(x = "technical effect, in replicate-SD units (posterior mean and 95% interval; pseudo-log axis)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
         title = "Instrument and other technical contrasts against their reference, every response"))
}
```

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=9}
if (!is.null(dec)) {
  dd <- dec[dec$term == "day" & is.finite(dec$z), ]
  dd$z_c <- pmax(pmin(dd$z, 3), -3)
  dd$mark <- ifelse(grepl("^detected", dd$verdict), ifelse(dd$positivity_flips %in% 0 | is.na(dd$positivity_flips), "●", as.character(dd$positivity_flips)), "")
  print(ggplot(dd, aes(level, response, fill = z_c)) + geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = .6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = mark), size = 2.6, colour = "#0b0b0b") +
    facet_grid(layer_f ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2a78d6", mid = "#f0f0ee", high = "#e34948", limits = c(-3, 3), name = "effect / replicate SD\n(capped at 3)") +
    thm + theme(legend.position = "right") +
    labs(x = "acquisition day", y = NULL, title = "Day effects; a dot marks an effect above replicate noise, a number the positivity calls it flips"))
}
```

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
if (!is.null(dec)) {
  fl <- dec[dec$term == "day" & !is.na(dec$positivity_flips) & dec$positivity_flips > 0, ]
  if (nrow(fl)) {
    fl$rule1 <- ifelse(grepl("^detected", fl$verdict), "above replicate noise", "within replicate noise")
    print(ggplot(fl, aes(level, positivity_flips, fill = rule1)) + geom_col(width = .7) +
      facet_grid(layer_f ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("above replicate noise" = "#e34948", "within replicate noise" = "#9a9a94")) + thm +
      labs(x = "acquisition day", y = "positivity calls flipped", fill = NULL,
           title = "Positivity calls that change when a day effect is removed (all responses, stacked)"))
  } else cat("no day effect flips a positivity call\n")
}
```

## Background (unstimulated) shifts

Layer BG: cytokine background in the neg tubes, as gate counts (`parent:gate`, logit scale) and as median intensity (`marker:median`, arcsinh units). Flips count stimulated calls that change when only the matched neg is shifted back.

```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}

if (!is.null(bg) && nrow(bg)) {

  print(knitr::kable(bg[bg$term == "day" & grepl("^detected", bg$verdict), setdiff(names(bg), c("layer_f", "z", "z_lo", "z_hi"))], digits = 3, caption = "Background: days above replicate noise", row.names = FALSE))
```

## Technical-marker assumption check

Layer A assumes the technical markers carry no biology. Each response is refitted with the protected covariates and time added; the plot shows estimate over standard error, the table the likelihood-ratio p values.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
ac <- rd("assumption_check.csv")
if (!is.null(ac)) {
  ac$zval <- ac$estimate / ac$se; ac$flag <- ifelse(ac$p_lrt < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "p >= 0.05")
  print(ggplot(ac, aes(zval, response, colour = flag, shape = flag)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#52514e") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-2, 2), linetype = 2, colour = "#9a9a94") + geom_point(size = 2.5) + facet_grid(. ~ covariate) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("p < 0.05" = "#eda100", "p >= 0.05" = "#9a9a94")) + scale_shape_manual(values = c("p < 0.05" = 17, "p >= 0.05" = 16)) +
    thm + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = .5)) +
    labs(x = "estimate / SE of the covariate in a technical-marker model", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL))
  knitr::kable(ac[, c("layer", "response", "covariate", "estimate", "se", "p_lrt")], digits = 4, caption = "Layer A refitted with the protected covariates: estimate, SE and likelihood-ratio p", row.names = FALSE)
} else cat("assumption_check.csv not present\n")
```

## Gate-position drift (were shifts hand-corrected by the analyst?)

Within a visit the unstimulated and stimulated tubes share one gate. Between acquisitions a gate that moves with the measured intensity shift means the analyst corrected the shift by hand; frequencies then look free of it, and the correction cannot be audited (Maecker et al. 2005; Welters et al. 2012; Finak et al. 2016). The fixed-threshold comparison under *Sensitivity analyses* shows what the frequencies look like without that adjustment.

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
gb <- rd("gate_bounds.csv")
if (!is.null(gb) && nrow(gb)) {
  if (!"gate_marker" %in% names(gb)) gb$gate_marker <- gb$parent   # files before 2026-10-13: parent gates only
  gb$position <- ifelse(is.na(gb$lower), gb$upper, gb$lower)
  gb <- merge(gb[!is.na(gb$position) & !is.na(gb$marker) & gb$marker == gb$gate_marker, ], tt[, c("filename", "acq_day", "instrument")], by = "filename")
  gb$gate <- ifelse(gb$gate_marker == gb$parent, paste(gb$parent, "gate"), paste(gb$parent, gb$gate_marker))
  print(ggplot(gb, aes(acq_day, position, colour = instrument)) + geom_point(alpha = .6, size = 1.8) +
    facet_wrap(~gate, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) + scale_colour_manual(values = pal_instr, drop = FALSE) + thm +
    labs(x = "acquisition day", y = "gate boundary on its own marker, arcsinh units", colour = NULL,
         title = "Where the analyst placed the parent and cytokine gates, per tube"))
}
g <- rd("gate_drift.csv"); if (!is.null(g)) knitr::kable(g, digits = 3) else cat("gate_bounds.csv empty: no rectangle/polygon gates found for the parent populations")
```

## Sensitivity analyses

From `15_sensitivity.R` and `06_biology.R` (docs/plans/drift_methods_review.md). Each table is also a CSV next to this report.

```{r sens-within-day, results="asis"}
wdf <- rd("week_slope_within_day.csv")
if (!is.null(wdf)) {
  cat("**Drift-free week slope.** On subject-days that carry several visits, week contrasts within the subject-day are immune to day, instrument and operator effects. The same tubes are fitted with the subject-day as a fixed effect (within day) and with subject and day as random intercepts (between day). These subject-days mostly hold the early visits, so the slope is a local one; what matters is whether the two estimators agree.\n\n")
  w <- reshape(wdf[, c("response", "estimator", "week_slope", "se")], idvar = "response", timevar = "estimator", direction = "wide")
  print(knitr::kable(w, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, caption = paste("Week slope, logit per year, on", wdf$n_tubes[1], "tubes of", wdf$n_subject_days[1], "subject-days")))
}
```

```{r sens-calendar, results="asis"}
}
```

## Fitting engines: brms against hand-written Stan, and BayesFlow

The correction question was fitted with brms and, as an independent implementation of the same model, with a hand-written Stan program. BayesFlow (amortised inference with neural networks) was tried on 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-24 and failed its acceptance checks both times (agreement with brms 0.94 and 0.76 against a gate of 0.95; its simulator did not reproduce the real unstimulated tubes). Its simulators know only instrument and day, not operator or the curved time term, so it was not rerun.

```{r engines-stan, fig.width=12, fig.height=9, results="asis"}
es <- plot_engine_stan(out)
if (!is.null(es)) { print(es$plot); print(knitr::kable(es$table, caption = "Stan estimate inside the brms 95 percent interval, per term", row.names = FALSE)) }
```

### BayesFlow results of the earlier run

```{r engines-bayesflow, fig.width=12, fig.height=7, results="asis"}
bh <- plot_bayesflow_history(out)
if (!is.null(bh)) {
  cat(sprintf("Full BayesFlow run of %s, on the model of that date (instrument and day only; no operator, straight-line week). v1 learns from tube summaries, v2 from single cells. Pass thresholds: calibration (SBC) and coverage for at least 90 percent of parameters, agreement with brms at least 0.95, and for v2 at least 85 percent of real tube medians inside the simulated 90 percent band.\n\n", bh$date))
  print(bh$plot)
  acc <- bh$acceptance; names(acc) <- c("variant", "calibration (SBC) ok", "coverage ok", "agreement with brms", "simulated tubes match real (v2)", "median recovery R2", "pass")
  print(knitr::kable(acc, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, caption = paste("BayesFlow acceptance checks, run of", bh$date)))
} else cat("No earlier BayesFlow results in this results folder.\n")
```
